elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(d) makes an Affiliate assignee the Depositor's successor, and Section 5.3 is expressly excepted from the general consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Sections 5.3(a) and (b) provide automatic succession for merger or consolidation transactions, and Section 5.3 is carved out from the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(c) broadly covers a Person succeeding to the Depositor's business, which encompasses a business acquisition, without requiring consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: A purchaser succeeding to the Depositor's business under Section 5.3(c) covers succession through a sale of substantially all business assets, and Section 5.3 is exempt from the consent requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The assignment provision requires, specifically for the Servicer, the Issuer's consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that the Issuer's consent for a Servicer assignment will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The added sentence categorically prohibits the Servicer from assigning the Agreement to a competitor of the Issuer or the Depositor.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right upon Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: No change-of-control termination right is granted, and Section 7.1 instead prohibits Servicer resignation unless the Servicer determines it is legally unable to perform.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3 provides automatic Depositor succession and is expressly excepted from the general assignment-consent restriction; no Servicer consent is required.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3 imposes post-transaction documentation and notice duties on the successor, but requires no written notice from the Depositor to the Servicer.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Although Section 7.6 describes Servicer successors, Section 7.6 was removed from the exceptions to the general assignment prohibition. A successor transaction implemented through an assignment therefore remains subject to Issuer consent.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 7.6 requires the successor—not the Servicer—to deliver certificates and an opinion to the Issuer and to notify Rating Agencies. It does not require the Servicer to give the Customer written notice.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: The general clause requires consents from trustees and specified securityholders for Depositor assignments, but it does not require the Servicer's consent.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: No Vendor consent right is stated for Depositor assignments, and there is consequently no operative restriction preventing the Vendor from unreasonably withholding such consent.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The general assignment provision expressly requires the Issuer's consent for a Servicer assignment.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that the Issuer's consent to a Servicer assignment will not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative redline reaches the preferred position by preserving the Depositor's Section 5.3 affiliate and successor rights, subjecting Servicer assignments to the Issuer's reasonable consent, prohibiting assignments to Customer-side competitors, and granting no change-of-control termination right. The changes are targeted and leave the preexisting third-party consent structure intact. The fallback is not fully satisfied because the clause is not mutual: it lacks Vendor consent for Customer's other assignments, lacks assignor-to-counterparty written-notice duties, and does not provide an unconditional Servicer successor-assignment right. Drafting quality is reduced by the tension between Section 7.6's automatic-successor wording and removal of its assignment carve-out, as well as the incomplete Section 7.1 fragment.
